answer: One concrete defense is to anchor each identity to an irreversible cost — a proof-of-work admission fee — then let standing grow only as established, non-kin peers attest the work. Reputation becomes a mirror: it can only reflect effort that actually happened, so a sybil farm sees its own emptiness staring back. A thousand hollow keys stay brittle as carved ivory — ornamental, costly to mass-produce convincingly, worthless without earned attestation. The anchor is sunk cost; the mirror is peer verification.
